summary: Rebuilt step M1-S02 and set it built again. The owning agent ran inline and changed two values in two files: the X-API-Key AuthHeader parameter gained parameterValue {!$Credential.OnCall_Tool_EC.ApiKey} (fixing S2-F-02, the org's 'The parameter type "AuthHeader" requires these fields: ParameterValue.'), and the Url parameter took the requester's real endpoint. The permission set and package.xml are byte-identical to run 1 by SHA-256, which is the evidence that S2-F-03 was a cascade rather than a defect. deploy-order.md gained a section 0 rebuild record and a rewritten section 5. Both declared checkers exit 0 verbatim from the build dir; check-outputs ok; five declared outputs, zero undeclared, zero relocations, nothing written outside artefacts/M1-S02.
confidence_rationale: Step 9 HIGH row is met on every clause: the step was legitimately claimable (gate re-signed on the amended inputs before the operator moved it to running), every required input of the owning agent resolved from plan.json, both envelopes validate, check-outputs exited 0, and nothing was written outside artefacts/M1-S02. The two unresolved inputs that held run 1 to MEDIUM are now bound by amendments[1].

process_observations.observation: The gate sequence was repaired correctly rather than worked around: the operator's own run record shows a sequencing error at 10:23:06Z, a step back to pending, the amendment, then a re-signed gate at 10:23:07Z before the step was claimed again.

The rebuild's blast radius is provable rather than asserted: the permission set and package.xml carry the same SHA-256 before and after, so the human-signed access review still applies to the exact bytes it was signed against.

Both declared checkers exited 0 against run 1's credential, which the org then rejected - no rule in either checker fires on an AuthHeader parameter missing parameterValue, so the step's automated test suite had no failure power over the defect that actually stopped the deploy.

Two facts a deployable credential cannot be written without - the endpoint URL and the name of the stored credential parameter - reached the build only after a failed dry run, across 45 clarifications and two verification rounds.

A5 is closed on the parameter name but the formula grammar is narrowed, not proven; a formula that parses and resolves to an empty string would pass mock-deploy run 2 and fail only at UAT, so the deploy checkpoint must not be read as the runtime one.

M1-S05's manual step 1 and the step's own manual clause (f) were written for a world where the formula was unwritten; clause (f) was updated in this step's artefacts, but M1-S05's prose belongs to another step and was left alone.
The step was already tested once, against artefacts two of which have since changed.
